caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 826 of 2005
lawyer:
N.H. Khandker, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner.
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
Md. Nazim Uddin ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Managing Director and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 170 of 1992 which subsequently being transferred on two occasions was numbered as the above Title Suit No. 71 of 1994, praying for permanent injunction on the averments that the suit land originally belonged to Nawab Court of Wards Estate, Dhaka and C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared. on 30.9.1935 Nawab Sir Salimullah and his brother Atiquallh gave pattan of the suit land to their grandsons Md. Habib and others by an "Amalnama" at a 'Salami' of Tk. 400/- and also delivered possession of the same to them; under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land, along with other land vested in the government, then on the prayer of Md. Habib and others the suit land was derequisitioned and vide Order No.27.6.1963 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1962 the suit land along with other plots were returned to them as choice land at a rent of Tk. 629.75 paisa and Md. Habib after getting back the suit land had been in peaceful possession of the same and after his death his only son Md. Hasan became the owner of the said land and he paid the rent regularly and S.A. and R.S. Khatians were prepared in his name; then Md. Hasan transferred the suit land to the plaintiff by registered Deed of Ewaj No.1592 on 12.5.1988 in exchange of his Gulshan land and also delivered possession of the suit land to the plaintiff; then after mutating his name the plaintiff had been possessing the suit land peacefully on paying rent and he also got the clearance from RAJUK for making construction but since the defendant was trying to dispossess him from the suit land on various pretext hence the suit. After filing of the above suit praying for permanent injunction the plaintiff also  filed an application praying for temporary injunction and obtained an order of status quo which the defendant No.1 opposed by filing written objection. It was the contention of the plaintiff that during the pendency of the order of status quo the defendant No.1 by violating the order of status quo dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land on 8.9.1992 and constructed building therein; the plaintiff then filed Violation Miscellaneous Case No.45 of 1992 which being transferred was renumbered as Violation Case No. 34 of 1994 in which 4 (four) witnesses have been examined and order is awaiting therein and the plaintiffs prayer for amendment of the  plaint incorporating therein the prayers for recovery of possession and also for mandatory injunction were allowed by orders dated 31.3.1996. The defendant contested the suit by filing a written State meat contending inter alia that there was no existence of the alleged suit land and that the S.A, R. S. and D.P. Khatian on which the plaintiff relied are false and fraudulent and moreover the suit, being barred by limitation, is also liable to be dismissed. The defendant also filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC for rejection of the plaint which on contest was rejected. In order to find out the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint and also its position an advocate commissioner was appointed for local investigation who after investigation submitted report with maps and the trial court also examined the advocate commissioner. In the trial the plaintiff deposed as P.W. 1 and proved many documents but the trial court out of those only marked Exts. 1-7 and did not allow the amalnama and the rent receipts to be exhibits; the trial court did not allow three witnesses to depose in favour of the plaintiff and also did not give any chance to the plaintiff to cross examine the witnesses of the defendants and also to argue the case for the plaintiff; thereafter without any consideration of the said violation miscellaneous case and the above Ext. Nos. 1-7 and also the report of the advocate commissioner, the trial court dismissed the suit. As against that the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 351 of 1999 but the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka after hearing, dismissed the appeal. The plaintiff then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 196 of 2000. The High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule holding that trial court on considering the materials on record dismissed the suit and the appellate Court, after discussing all aspects of the case dismissed the appeal and the courts below did not commit any illegality.
